# TASK-168 — specification

## Scope

Essentials per project type: the essential questions follow the project type. A library drops sign-in (security.3) and environments (delivery.1) for its public API (data.9) and packaging (delivery.8); a device drops sign-in for its test matrix (testing.9) and packaging; mobile and desktop add packaging; a data or AI system adds model evaluation (testing.10). Web applications and APIs keep the 15. Every added question applies to the type and is already required at the complete level, so essentials stay a subset of complete, and every type keeps the same nine sections to review.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] (2026-10-09) The essentials follow the project type through `essentialIdsFor`: swaps only, each to a question that applies to the type and is already required at the complete level, with the same nine sections under review (15 or 16 questions per type).

## Verification

- tests/essentials.test.ts
- tests/minimal-spec.test.ts
- new-project.test.tsx

## Notes

`essentialIdsFor`, `essentialCount`, `isEssential(id, type)`, `levelHelp` in `shared/essentials.ts`; `moduleQuestions`; the draft prompt; the new-project dialog and Settings counts. No migration (derived from `level` and `projectType`). Tests: `tests/essentials.test.ts` (17), `tests/minimal-spec.test.ts` (a library approves with its own list and is refused with the web list), `new-project.test.tsx`. Deviation from the plan: devices use testing.9, because security.10 is optional in the library and the essentials level can only lower requirements.
